header: The US dollar in rupees over the last year (the chart under the currency converter, shown when the converter is on USD and INR). The source is Frankfurter, which publishes the European Central Bank's reference rates: one rate for every working day (the ECB does not publish on weekends and its holidays), the same table the converter's own rate comes from, so the last point of the chart is the rate the converter shows. A reference rate is the ECB's daily fixing, not the rate of a bank or a money changer, and not the RBI's. Self-check, so that a changed answer is a loud error and never a wrong number: the dates must be real and in order, every rate must be plausible, the record must reach back to one year before its last day, and it must be fresh. A failure throws, and the route then returns the last good answer (marked as such) or a plain failure; I guess nothing.

members.name: carried
doc: Set on the first point when the ECB published no rate on that exact day (a weekend or a holiday): it holds the day of the rate it really is (the last working day before).

symbols.name: rangeStart
symbols.sig: export function rangeStart(now: DateTime = DateTime.now().setZone(ZONE)): string
doc: Where the year starts: a few days before the anniversary, so that the working day on or after it is always inside the answer.

symbols.name: parseUsdInr
symbols.sig: export function parseUsdInr(json: unknown, now: DateTime = DateTime.now().setZone(ZONE)): RatePoint[]
doc: This reads Frankfurter's answer for a range ({"rates":{"2025-11-10":{"INR":88.68}, ...}}) into the working days of the year that ends on its last day (the day a year before it, or the working day after it, to the last). `now` fixes today for the tests.

symbols.name: validUsdInr
symbols.sig: export function validUsdInr(t: UsdInrTrend | null | undefined): t is UsdInrTrend

behaviours: the request starts six days before the anniversary, so that the working day on or after it is inside
the year is the 255 working days from 13 Nov 2025 (the same date a year before today, 13 Nov 2026) to 12 Nov 2026 (the latest the ECB has published), in date order
the rate on this day a year ago (13 Nov 2025) is 88.69 and the latest is 94.04
the highest is 96.83 on 20 May 2026 and the lowest 88.50 on 19 Nov 2025
the days before the anniversary that the request carried are dropped
when the anniversary is a Saturday (15 Nov 2025, today 15 Nov 2026) the chart begins on that date with the rate of Friday 14 Nov, marked as carried; the next point is the Monday
a working-day anniversary needs no carrying
a valid trend is accepted; a short or unordered one is not
the days are sorted whatever the order of the answer
not an object of rates is refused
an implausible rate (9.4) is refused
a day without a rupee rate is refused
a day that is not a date is refused
a stale record (latest day more than a week old) is refused
a record that is only a few days old is accepted (a weekend)
a record shorter than a year is refused
a hole of more than a week in the record is refused
a record that begins well after the anniversary is refused
the route reads nothing from the caller (no request, no cookies, no headers) and asks one fixed Frankfurter address
the status page asks it too
